posts.author: eric343
posts.post_subject: Coherent Compass 315M laser used for DCG holgraphy?
posts.content_md: It has a coherence length of ~100 meters thanks to a ring-cavity design. No kidding... it's one of the diode lasers everyone recommends for holography.

posts.topic_title: Coherent Compass 315M laser used for DCG holgraphy?
posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.post_subject: Coherent Compass 315M laser used for DCG holgraphy?
posts.content_md:
They work well for holography. The coherence length is closer to 50M and actually it is not a ring cavity even though that was what was assumed for a long time. 

Here are a couple of links of interest:

[http://www.kellerstudio.de/repairfaq/sa ... tm#sslc315](http://www.kellerstudio.de/repairfaq/sam/laserssl.htm#sslc315)

[http://www.kellerstudio.de/repairfaq/sa ... m#sslc315f](http://www.kellerstudio.de/repairfaq/sam/laserssl.htm#sslc315f)

well it looks as if a deal has been made! i talked to sal at mr.gizmos

The following are just some of what's included in this unit:

Coherent C315M-100 green DPSS laser head with Coeherent analog 

controller. The laser head has been adjusted to produce at least 100 mW. 

Polarization rotator (waveplate type, 0-360 degrees) with gear driven stepper motor control and position sensor. 

Various lenses and other optics, some adjustable via stepper motors. 

High speed Acouto Optic Modulator (AOM) (no driver).

posts.topic_title: Coherent Compass 315M laser used for DCG holgraphy?
posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.post_subject: Coherent Compass 315M laser used for DCG holgraphy?
posts.content_md: Yeah, It has a tunning program that makes it flicker and change brightness until both LEDs on the test connector are lit. After running mine overnight the laser heatsink is quite cool, at least with a 70F ambient. The controller was quite hot and I will be mounting it to it's own heatsink. 108 watts is a little underpowered for the warm up cycle but it should be fine. Coherent recommends 150 watts and Laser Sam uses a 80 watt supply.

posts.content_md:
hello all ,

ive been very buzy this weekend ! my laminar flow booth is almost finished(ill try to post some picture of its construction). this 315 laser is a fantistic holography tool ! i have to thank bruce for e mailing the pictures of his 315 laser (really nice set up). i am about to reset up my lab so i am able to bring this laser into light and take a few pictures........

![Image](http://members.aol.com/holoart/315laser1.jpg)

the laser is hot glued to the platform and a small project box with a portion of the side cutaway(also hot glued in place), to make box draw air through the fins and out the mini box fan.

with the small fan running the laser stays very cool so the hot glue is not likely melt !

![Image](http://members.aol.com/holoart/315laser2.jpg)

the shutter is a take out from the original box of parts the laser came with.

its a ac 12v plus shutter, i plugged it into a small wall/plug type transformer, and attached a new ,from Stanley ,a remote switch made for turning on/off x-mass lights ,so now my shutter is wireless!

i was able to shoot a couple of test shots in DCG and see how great this laser really is!

![Image](http://members.aol.com/holoart/DCGholo4.jpg)

the above image plane holo was about a 2 min exp.

i did a 5x7 test and got a exp. in excess of 8 min!
